name: Example Steadybrook Pantry Foods (fictional)
summary: A fictional food maker with slow, steady growth of about 2% a year. It turns most of its profit into cash, pays out roughly three quarters of its profit as dividends, and trades on a low P/E.
assumptions: All figures are fictional and in millions of USD, except the share price. The same tax rate (25% of pre-tax profit), tax rules and accounting apply to every company. No one-off items, share issues or buybacks. Ratios use Year 3 and the current share price. Simulated for learning; not a real firm.
notes: Operating cash flow is higher than net income every year, and free cash flow comfortably covers the dividend.
Return on capital of about 21% suggests the business earns well on the money tied up in it, under these fictional figures.
Slow growth: the low P/E may reflect that buyers expect little growth. A high payout leaves less to reinvest.
Risk to watch: a cheaper rival or a change in what shoppers want could squeeze the steady margin.
